analysis.investment_thesis: A 2022-incorporated micro-cap jeweler with essentially zero profitability (ROE 0.12%) trading at 17x earnings is speculation, not investment. No moat, no track record, no margin of safety — I'd pass without hesitation.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 60.18% provides skin-in-the-game alignment
Operates in a large, enduring category (Indian gems & jewellery)
Small base theoretically allows high percentage growth if execution works
key_risks: ROE of 0.12% indicates the business barely earns its cost of capital — or anything
Incorporated only 2022; no proven track record across a cycle
Jewellery is a commoditized, working-capital-heavy industry with no brand moat at this scale
red_flags: P/E of 17x on 0.12% ROE is absurdly disconnected from earning power
Micro-cap (INR 88.6 Cr) recently listed SME-style jeweller — classic speculative pocket
Negligible institutional ownership (FII 1.39%) suggests no serious diligence has validated the story
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my chair, this fails nearly every test. I want businesses that consistently earn 15%+ on equity with durable moats — Retaggio earns 0.12%, meaning shareholders' capital is essentially idle. Paying 17x earnings for a four-year-old jeweller with no brand, no scale, and no demonstrated capital-allocation record is speculating on a story, not buying a business. The jewellery industry in India is dominated by trusted regional brands (Titan/Tanishq, Kalyan, Malabar) that took decades to build customer trust; a 2022 entrant has no structural advantage.

Margin of safety is absent: the market cap of INR 88.6 Cr implies expectations far beyond current earnings power, and a 60% promoter holding in a newly-listed micro-cap means liquidity and governance risk both sit on the shareholder's side of the ledger. I'd need years of 15%+ ROE, stable margins, and honest capital allocation before even studying this. Until then, this is firmly in the "too hard / no thank you" pile.
